name: moving stones

attributes.attribute: the belief that old stones could move about at will
the stones that went to a lake or river to drink
the stones that turned to dancing form, like at Merry Maidens

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Moving stones are part of folk belief in the Celtic lands. The land is full of signs of a folk that came before the Celts. That early folk raised rings of stone and works of mystery that no one has read. Many tales hang on these old places, though none can trace their first root. One tale says that the stones were not set fast in the earth. They could move about at will. The move came at midnight, or at dawn, and only on a great day of the year. The day could be the summer solstice or Samhain, the old fall feast. The stones rose from their bed and crossed the land. Often they went to a nearby lake or river to bathe and drink. Some turned to dancing stones, like those of Merry Maidens. When the hour of their freedom passed, they went back to their own place.
